narratives.Description: Flip #1419 agentic-prioritization gates from advisory to enforce mode (advise -> observe -> block)
narratives.Overview:
## Context

The Agentic Prioritization & Coordination Model (#1419) shipped across 7 delivery slices. Per the agreed **advise -> observe -> block** rollout discipline, every new gate/dial landed **ADVISORY** on directive itself:

- `task verify:capacity` (Slice 4, PR #1503) -- three-state but advisory; NOT in the `task check` aggregate; never fails the build closed.
- `task verify:judgment-gates` (Slice 3, PR #1504) -- risk-tiered engine + four default-on universal safety gates (secrets / prod-infra / AGENTS.md+skills / installer); advisory by default; NOT in `task check`; an `--enforce` fail-closed posture is implemented + unit-tested but opt-in only.
- Earned-autonomy dial (Slice 5, PR #1505) -- advisory recommendation only; a human confirms any level flip; never auto-reduces required clearances.
- Gate-0 / `task swarm:launch` gate-clearance integration (Slice 7, PR #1507) -- advisory by default (an uncleared block-tier gate is surfaced but the launch proceeds); `--enforce` / `--enforce-gates` fails closed.

## Why this was deferred

Flipping to block-mode on day one risks self-DoS on the framework's own repo: a single false-positive gate would block every commit / PR / dispatch -- including the change needed to fix the gate. The flip is intentionally gated on an **observation window** where real data accrues: `minSampleSize` classified completions for capacity, override-rate / rework-rate history for the autonomy dial, and judgment-gate false-positive rates.

## Future work (this issue)

After an observation window, decide **per gate** whether to flip directive itself from advisory to enforce/block:

- [ ] Capacity: decide whether `verify:capacity` enters the `task check` aggregate and/or `capacityAllocation.enforcement: block`.
- [ ] Judgment gates: enable the enforce posture for the default-on universal safety gates and wire `verify:judgment-gates` into `task check` / `.githooks/pre-push`.
- [ ] Autonomy dial: decide whether the recommended level auto-applies once override / false-positive rates stay low over the window (this also resolves the Open Questions v2 autonomy-ratchet-threshold item).
- [ ] Gate-0 / `swarm:launch`: turn on `--enforce-gates` by default for block-tier gates on directive.
- [ ] Preserve emergency escape hatches (env-var / `--allow-*` bypass) and document each flip in AGENTS.md + the relevant skills.

## Acceptance

- A per-gate enforce/advisory decision is recorded together with the observation data that justified it.
- Any gate flipped to block carries an env-var / `--allow-*` emergency bypass and is documented.
- The flip lands **incrementally** (one gate at a time), each validated against directive's own tree before merge.

Refs #1419. Follow-up to delivery-slice PRs #1503, #1504, #1505, #1507.

issue: deftai/directive#1511
charter: open critique
spend: N≥3
round: 1
critic-role: fresh
id-ceiling: 5956221730
dispatch-sha: af82911053eb0bbb57b523823715e99633e16772
arc-mode: no-ingest
audit-targets: none

## Inputs honored
- Stop 1: 5956201809
- panel-deposit: 5956221730
- pin-read only at dispatch-sha; no later siblings

## Pain dispositions

### pain: P1 — Observation contract unbound
disposition: supported
class: blocks-the-design

Evidence (pin af82911053eb0bbb57b523823715e99633e16772):
- Issue Acceptance demands a per-gate enforce/advisory decision "together with the observation data that justified it," but names no schema, sink path, sample floor, or FP/override/rework thresholds that would make that decision falsifiable.
- Capacity `minSampleSize` (default 20 in `packages/core/src/validate-content/capacity-policy.ts`) only keeps `verify:capacity` advisory until enough *classified completions* accrue (`packages/core/src/validate-content/verify-capacity.ts` returns exit 0 while `report.advisoryMode`). That is an accounting cold-start guard, not a flip-to-enforce observation contract. Flip is a bare `capacityAllocation.enforcement: advise|enforce` field with no observation predicate binding the write.
- Autonomy dial thresholds exist (`DEFAULT_AUTONOMY_MIN_SAMPLE_SIZE`, `advance_override_max`, `retreat_override_rate`, `rework_baseline` in `packages/core/src/policy/autonomy.ts`) and consume `override_rate` from `pending-human-decisions.jsonl` via `packages/core/src/policy/decisions.ts` / `capacity/show.ts`. Those metrics drive `recommendAutonomyLevel` only (`advisory: true` on every return). They are not bound as a gate for flipping `verify:*` or Gate-0 to enforce.
- Judgment-gate FP / fire / clearance rates have no dedicated telemetry sink under `packages/core/src/orchestration/`; `verify-judgment-gates.ts` evaluates presence/shape/authority of clearances and exits 0 unless `--enforce`. No observation-window ledger for false-positive rate appears at pin.
- SPECIFICATION Open Questions v2 still lists "Autonomy ratchet metric: exact signal + thresholds" as open research — the flip issue inherits that unbound metric space.

Failure mode: an operator (or agent) can flip enforce citing "observation window done" without a checkable bar; the deferral's measurement premise collapses into judgment-call prose.

Disposition consequence: any Bound for #1511 must bind per-gate observation predicates (sample size, FP/override/rework ceilings, durable sinks, recorded flip artifact) before the first enforce land. Unbound observation keeps the issue unsafe to implement as written.

### pain: P2 — Aggregate coupling / self-DoS
disposition: supported
class: blocks-the-design

Evidence:
- `tasks/verify.yml` documents both `verify:capacity` and `verify:judgment-gates` as DELIBERATELY NOT in the `task check` aggregate ("must never fail-closed on the framework tree").
- Root `Taskfile.yml` capacity include comment repeats that deliberate absence.
- `.githooks/pre-push` runs only `preflight-gh --pre-push-stdin`; it does not invoke judgment-gates or capacity.
- Issue Future work proposes wiring judgment-gates into `task check` / `.githooks/pre-push` and defaulting Gate-0 `--enforce-gates` after the window — the exact aggregate coupling the deferral avoided — while Acceptance only gestures at "env-var / `--allow-*` emergency bypass" without an inventory of which bypasses exist for these gates.
- At pin, `packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts` parses `--enforce-gates` into `enforceGatesFlag`, computes `gatePosture = enforce|advise`, then `void gatePosture`. The flag is live on the CLI (`launch-cli.ts`) but the judgment-clearance posture is discarded; Gate-0 enforce is not a working fail-closed path for uncleared block-tier gates via that flag.
- Separate `enforceGates()` in the same file is the preflight/readiness gate stack, not the judgment-gate clearance posture. No `DEFT_ALLOW_*` / `--allow-*` pair specific to capacity or judgment-gate flips appears beside the established bypass patterns for branch / bot-merge / destructive-gh.

Failure mode: landing capacity or judgment-gates into `task check` / pre-push (or defaulting `--enforce-gates`) on a false positive wedges every commit/PR/dispatch, including the fix PR — the day-one self-DoS the advisory rollout was designed to avoid. The missing bypass inventory and the dead `gatePosture` make an all-at-once or default-on flip especially brittle.

Disposition consequence: Bound must require (1) per-gate emergency bypass inventory before aggregate wiring, (2) incremental one-gate landings validated on directive's own tree, (3) no default `--enforce-gates` until launch actually consumes posture (repair the void), and (4) refuse coupling multiple flips into one check/pre-push change.

### pain: P3 — Autonomy dial vs clearance
disposition: supported
class: blocks-the-design

Evidence:
- Issue checklist item: decide whether the recommended autonomy level "auto-applies" once override / false-positive rates stay low — explicitly the Open Questions v2 autonomy-ratchet-threshold item.
- Current implementation is advisory-only end-to-end: `recommendAutonomyLevel` hard-codes `advisory: true`; advance rationale states the next level "would reduce required human clearances" and "ADVISORY: a human confirms; no auto-ratchet" (`packages/core/src/policy/autonomy.ts`). Surface is `task capacity:show` render (`capacity/show.ts` "Autonomy dial (advisory-only)").
- `plan.policy.autonomy.gates` / `gate_levels` can store per-gate levels, but the recommendation path does not write policy or clearances. Auto-apply is absent today and is exactly what #1511 puts on the table.
- Conflating dial advance with clearance reduction would silently lower `requiredHumanReviewers` / block-tier obligations without a separate clearance event — the hazard Stop 1 names.

Failure mode: a clean observation window auto-writes a more permissive autonomy level; subsequent launches proceed with fewer human clearances than the prior policy required, with no independent override/false-positive gate on the clearance reduction itself.

Disposition consequence: Bound must keep a hard wall between dial recommendation and clearance authority. Auto-apply of recommended level must not mutate required clearances; any clearance reduction needs a separate human-confirmed clearance/policy write, or the issue must drop auto-apply and keep recommend-only.

## Stress — Bound-remedy options (open critique; no Prefer-A bind map)

### 1. Observation contract
Bind, per gate, before any enforce land:
- `minSampleSize` (and what is counted: classified completions vs resolved clearances vs launch advisories).
- Max false-positive / override / rework rates that authorize a flip.
- Durable telemetry sinks (extend `xbrief/.audit/` receipts and/or an explicit observation ledger; do not rely on chat or issue prose).
- A recorded flip-decision artifact citing those numbers (Acceptance's "decision + observation data" made checkable).

Without this, incremental flips still rest on unfalsifiable claims.

### 2. Incremental one-gate landings + emergency bypasses
- Inventory env-var and `--allow-*` bypasses for each candidate gate *before* wiring into `task check` / pre-push / default launch.
- Land one gate at a time; validate on directive's tree; document in AGENTS.md + relevant skills as Acceptance already requires.
- Repair Gate-0 so `--enforce-gates` actually consumes `gatePosture` (today: `void gatePosture` at `swarm/launch.ts`) before any default-on decision.
- Keep capacity and judgment-gates out of the check aggregate until each has a working bypass and a green observation window under the bound contract.

### 3. Autonomy dial vs clearance wall
- Prefer keep-recommend-only: dial remains advisory forever for clearance count; human confirms any `plan.policy.autonomy` write.
- If auto-apply is still desired, split into two motions: (a) dial may auto-update a *recommendation* field; (b) clearance reduction requires a separate typed clearance / policy mutation with its own override/FP gate — never a silent side effect of (a).
- Do not resolve OQ autonomy-ratchet by collapsing dial advance into fewer `requiredHumanReviewers`.

## Additional classified findings

### F1. Gate-0 `--enforce-gates` posture is dead at pin
class: sharpens-framing
Evidence: `launch-cli.ts` sets `enforceGatesFlag`; `launch.ts` assigns `gatePosture` then `void gatePosture`.
Failure mode: issue text and CHANGELOG describe opt-in enforce for uncleared block-tier gates; operators may believe `--enforce-gates` already fail-closes when it does not.
Disposition consequence: sharpen Future-work Gate-0 item to include "make enforce posture live" before "default on." Supports P2; does not replace it.

### F2. Companion #1517 is closed completed (footnote)
class: footnote
REST `issues/1517` is `state: closed` with completed brief `xbrief/completed/2026-09-29-1517-…` at pin. Stop 1 listed it under related. No pain weight; do not treat merge-gate-enforcement (#1517) as an open blocker for this arc.

## Road not taken
- Claiming P1 overclaimed because capacity/autonomy already have `minSampleSize`: rejected — those floors activate accounting/recommendations, not the advisory→enforce flip decision #1511 asks for.
- Treating P2 as footnote because Acceptance already says "incremental" + bypasses: rejected — Acceptance names the goals without binding bypass inventory, one-gate validation order, or the dead Gate-0 posture; the self-DoS path remains open in the Future-work checklist as written.

## Steelman (rejected)
Strongest reject of P3: "the issue only asks to *decide* whether auto-apply happens; it does not mandate auto-apply, so the clearance wall is already safe." Flip: the checklist puts auto-apply on the solution menu without a hard forbid; without an explicit wall in Bound, implementers can ship auto-apply as the natural reading of "flip … to enforce mode" plus the OQ ratchet item. That is enough for blocks-the-design on the issue as a build contract.

## Summary
P1, P2, and P3 are all supported with pin-read mechanisms. The safe Bound space is: bind observation predicates + sinks first; land one gate at a time with named emergency bypasses and a live Gate-0 enforce path; keep autonomy dial recommendations behind a clearance wall (no silent clearance reduction).

issue: deftai/directive#1511
charter: open critique
spend: N≥3
round: 1
critic-role: fresh
id-ceiling: 5956221730
dispatch-sha: af82911053eb0bbb57b523823715e99633e16772
arc-mode: no-ingest
audit-targets: none

The flip needs an explicit per-gate admission decision, not a global change of defaults. Existing thresholds and audit records are real, but they do not establish measured readiness to enforce. There is also a missing execution connection and a weak clearance acceptance boundary to resolve before claiming enforcement.

Method: independently read source using `git show af82911053eb0bbb57b523823715e99633e16772:<path>`. Thread inputs were only Stop 1 (5956201809) and panel-deposit (5956221730). This is static mechanism verification, not executed fixture coverage or measured production false-positive data. All source anchors below refer to that SHA. The deposit matches the envelope ceiling and names three families; panel completeness is not observable within this envelope.

### P1: overclaimed as blanket absence; the promotion-evidence gap is supported

**sharpens-framing** - Thresholds and sinks already exist. `packages/core/src/policy/autonomy.ts` defines sample 20, advance override maximum 0.05, retreat override threshold 0.2, and rework baseline 0.15. The pinned project policy explicitly configures capacity sample 20 and window 30. `validate-content/verify-capacity.ts::evaluate` retains advisory behavior below the sample threshold even under enforce. `orchestration/verify-judgment-gates.ts::recordClearance` appends durable JSONL records; `capacity/show.ts::computeReport` consumes decision-backlog override/P0 signals and completion rework. Rebuilding these as absent would create competing policy and accounting surfaces. Consequence: narrow P1 to the missing per-gate observation-to-promotion contract; do not equate existing dial defaults with approved promotion thresholds.

**blocks-the-design** - Existing samples measure different things. Capacity counts classified completions; the autonomy call uses `backlog.resolved_in_window`, project-wide override rate, and completion rework, without a gate id. Neither call proves how often a particular gate would wrongly block. A high-volume easy gate can mask an unobserved rare gate; repeated evaluations of one change can also inflate a new naive telemetry sample. A binding remedy must name the independent decision unit, per-gate denominator, observation window and policy version, adjudicated false-positive numerator, override reasons distinct from false positives, missing-data behavior, sink, and explicit promote/hold/rollback decision. Insufficient or unclassified evidence must hold promotion. Reuse existing records where adequate; add only the missing outcome/evaluation linkage. Do not invent numeric acceptance thresholds from the defaults.

### P2: supported as a proposed rollout risk, not an existing aggregate outage

**blocks-the-design** - `validate-content/verify-capacity.ts::evaluate` blocks on historical bucket deficit above tolerance 1.0 without receiving a candidate change. Wiring that result into every commit/check can reject the very work intended to repair the deficit: history cannot improve until work completes. `tasks/verify.yml` explicitly excludes judgment gates from `task check`; `.githooks/pre-push` invokes `preflight-gh`, rather than these gates directly. Consequence: do not bind a universal aggregate flip. Prefer capacity enforcement at work admission, or explicitly prove how corrective work remains admissible. Stage one named gate at one named entry point, with an actual blocking case, unaffected case, correction-path case, and recovery case before expanding.

**blocks-the-design** - A flag-default flip is not the promised launch enforcement. `swarm/launch-cli.ts` parses `--enforce-gates`; `swarm/launch.ts:1342-1343` computes `gatePosture` and immediately discards it with `void gatePosture`. The separate `enforceGates` function runs preflight/readiness independently and does not receive this posture. Consequence: require an end-to-end test that an otherwise admissible story with an uncleared targeted gate is refused before launch side effects, while the advisory case proceeds. Preserve the existing readiness checks. Do not count parser coverage as gate enforcement.

**sharpens-framing** - Inventory existing controls before adding escape hatches: capacity `enforcement: advise`, judgment's opt-in `--enforce`, `judgmentGatesDisabled` filtering in `effectiveGates`, and scope-keyed clearance JSONL. These are not interchangeable emergency bypasses. A clearance says the requirement was satisfied; an emergency exception says it was not. The rollout should name a narrow, operator-authorized, auditable recovery path, its scope and expiry, and demonstrate that it works while the new gate is red. Avoid a global skip-all-gates switch or routine rewriting of targets to clear failures.

### P3: overclaimed as current behavior; preserve the existing separation

**sharpens-framing** - `policy/autonomy.ts::recommendAutonomyLevel` returns `advisory: true` on advance, hold, and retreat; advancement explicitly says human confirmation and no auto-ratchet. Its production callers are report builders (`capacity/show.ts` and `validate-content/capacity-show.ts`). This evidence does not establish current silent clearance reduction. Consequence: keep recommendations advisory in this enforcement slice and explicitly preserve required clearances independent of the dial. Auto-application would be a separate authority change needing its own evidence and acceptance contract; better statistics alone do not authorize fewer reviewers.

**blocks-the-design** - The clearance wall itself needs a concrete acceptance rule before being presented as human authorization. In `orchestration/verify-judgment-gates.ts`, `outcomeCleared` checks only non-null clearance; `lookupClearance` accepts a matching gate id and evidence hash. `recordClearance` permits empty reviewers and caller-supplied actor; acceptance does not enforce `required_human_reviewers`. `fingerprintScope` hashes matched evidence, such as path names, not file contents or a candidate revision. Thus the same paths can retain clearance after content changes, and a locally supplied record can satisfy a gate advertised as requiring a human. Consequence: bind clearance validity to the intended candidate/policy scope and an independently established authorized approval source, enforce required reviewer eligibility/count, and refuse stale or untrusted records. The injection/swarm failure is promoting worker-controlled labels, body text, or JSONL actor claims into authority; concurrent worktrees must not inherit approval merely because their path lists match. If human authorization is outside this slice, narrow the enforcement claim explicitly instead of implying this log provides it.

Road not taken: a single global switch is operationally simple and avoids inconsistent entry points. Its strongest case is that all gates share a trustworthy evaluator, adequate gate-specific observations, and a demonstrated recovery path. The pinned mechanisms do not establish those premises. Evidence of them, including correction-path and stale-clearance tests, could justify broader rollout later. For now, incremental admission enforcement with the autonomy dial left advisory is the smaller defensible option; this critique does not bind a Prefer-A map.

verification-path: pin-read `git show af82911053eb0bbb57b523823715e99633e16772:` ; dest cwd-without-occupy. All anchors below are re-derived at that SHA via `git show` / `git grep`, not read from the issue or the triage.

## Inventory before proposing

Three existing mechanisms the Bound remedy should reuse rather than reinvent:

1. **Emergency-bypass family.** `DEFT_ALLOW_*` is already the established form: `DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT`, `DEFT_ALLOW_COVERAGE_DEBT`, `DEFT_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_GH_VERBS`, `DEFT_ALLOW_RELEASE_PUBLISH`, `DEFT_ALLOW_BOT_MERGE`, `DEFT_ALLOW_ISSUE_CLOSE`, plus `DEFT_SESSION_RITUAL_SKIP`. Acceptance bullet 2 should name reuse of this family, not a new bypass shape.
2. **Check-composition contract.** `REQUIRED_CONSUMER_ENFORCEMENT_GATES` (`packages/core/src/consumer-check-contract/evaluate.ts:24`) plus `verify:consumer-check-contract` (`tasks/verify.yml:401`) already enforce which gates a check aggregate must carry. "Enters the `task check` aggregate" is one list entry there; no new composition mechanism is needed, and that list is also where an incremental landing order would be legible.
3. **Three-state posture convention.** 0 clean / 1 violation / 2 config is already the shape of both `verify:capacity` (`tasks/verify.yml:598`) and `verify:judgment-gates` (`tasks/verify.yml:615`).

## Pain disposition

| Pain | Disposition |
|---|---|
| P1 observation contract unbound | **supported**, but the premise is wrong in a way that would misdirect the remedy — see F6 |
| P2 aggregate coupling / self-DoS | **supported and understated** — see F4, and F5 inverts the risk statement |
| P3 autonomy dial vs clearance | **overclaimed** as stated — see F2; the guarded path does not exist |

---

### F1 — `blocks-the-design` — the judgment-gate engine has no firing log, so the false-positive rate AC-1 depends on is uncomputable

**Evidence.** In `packages/core/src/orchestration/verify-judgment-gates.ts` the only durable write in the module is the `appendFileSync` at L277, inside `recordClearance` (L222). `buildReport` (L515) and `evaluate` (L594) compute `outcomes` and hand them to `renderReport` (L561) or JSON stdout; nothing persists a firing. `readClearances` (L199) is the only reader of durable state. The sink itself, `xbrief/.audit/judgment-gate-clearances.jsonl`, holds exactly **one** record at the dispatch SHA, timestamped `2026-06-08T19:44:18Z` — roughly four months before dispatch, against gates that landed 2026-06-04.

**Failure mode.** A false-positive rate is wrong-firings over firings. The clearance log is a sample of *cleared* firings only, and its records carry no right/wrong label (`clearance_id`, `timestamp`, `gate_id`, `cleared_scope`, `reviewers`, `actor`, `reason`). An observation window of any length produces a partial numerator and no denominator at all. The quantity the issue names cannot be computed from this tree.

**Disposition consequence.** AC-1 — "a per-gate enforce/advisory decision is recorded **together with the observation data that justified it**" — is not satisfiable for judgment gates as the gate is built. A decision recorded against this sink would be an attestation, not a measurement. The lean must either land an outcome log (fired / cleared / cleared-then-reverted) before the window opens, or drop FP rate as the judgment-gate criterion and state what replaces it.

### F2 — `blocks-the-design` — the autonomy dial's only input log has no writer anywhere in the tree

**Evidence.** `recommendAutonomyLevel` (`packages/core/src/policy/autonomy.ts:195`) takes `override_rate`, `rework_rate`, `sample_size` from its caller. ## Bound-remedy stress (open critique — options, not a bind map)

**(a) Observation contract.** The sharpest version is not a thresholds document; thresholds exist (F6). It is: *per gate, name the producer that writes the denominator, and refuse to open the window until that producer is landed and emitting.* Judgment gates need an outcome log, not the clearance log (F1). Autonomy needs the decision-event producer (F2). Capacity needs nothing. Cost: two producer stories ahead of the window. Buys: AC-1 becomes satisfiable rather than attestable. The rejected alternative is running the window on clearance records alone and reading "no complaints" as clean — that fails because `verify:judgment-gates` is in no aggregate (`tasks/verify.yml:615` says so in its own description) and has one record in four months, so absence of records is indistinguishable from the gate never having run.

**(b) Incremental one-gate landings with bypasses.** The granularity AC-3 names does not exist in the code. `verify:judgment-gates` evaluates all four universal gates in one invocation; posture is a single `--enforce` over the whole report, and `reportBlocking` filters by `tier`/`class`, not by gate id. There is no per-gate posture field. So "one gate at a time" needs a choice the lean should make explicitly: add a per-gate posture map under `plan.policy.judgmentGates`; or sequence by **surface** (pre-push, then `task check` via `REQUIRED_CONSUMER_ENFORCEMENT_GATES`, then PR) rather than by gate; or sequence by narrowing the universal glob sets. On bypasses: reuse `DEFT_ALLOW_*` rather than inventing a form — but per F4, a bypass needed on every push is not an emergency hatch, so the bypass decision is downstream of the clearance-scope decision and cannot stand in for it.

**(c) Autonomy dial vs clearance wall.** At the pin the wall is absolute and costless: `advisory: true` on every branch, no persisted level, `gate_levels` read by nothing. Framing this as "dial vs wall" presumes the wall is load-bearing; it currently guards a door with no room behind it. The two honest options are (i) strike auto-apply from this issue and keep the dial as display-only, documenting that the recommendation has no consumer, or (ii) land level persistence plus a clearance-requirement consumer as a separate issue, and only then ask the auto-apply question — at which point P3's concern becomes real and worth a gate, which it is not today.

## Road not taken

I considered classifying F3 as `sharpens-framing` on the reading that `void gatePosture` is a deliberate placeholder for an unlanded slice, making checkbox 4 merely premature rather than wrong. I kept `blocks-the-design` because the issue body asserts the advisory behaviour as *shipped* ("an uncleared block-tier gate is surfaced but the launch proceeds"), and a lean binding on that sentence would open an observation window over a surface that observes nothing and then read the resulting silence as a clean record.

## Steelman

The strongest rejected position: *these are four advisory gates that cost nothing today; flip them one at a time, watch, roll back if it hurts — the critique over-engineers a reversible change.* That holds for `verify:capacity`, which has a bound window, a sample floor, 1215 classified completions, and a documented reason it sits outside `task check`. It fails for the other three not on rigour but on availability: there is nothing to watch, and a rollback signal requires a signal.

**What would flip my verdict:** a producer outside this tree — a CI artifact, a hosted log, an ops dashboard — that records judgment-gate firings and human decisions. My recorded verification path is pin-read, so an out-of-tree sink is beyond what I can observe. If one exists, F1 and F2 drop to `sharpens-framing` (the sink is real but undocumented on the issue, and AC-1 should name it), while F3, F4, F5 and F6's per-gate asymmetry are unaffected — they are read off the code, not off the data.

## In plain English

Four gates shipped as advice. This issue proposes flipping them to blocking after watching them for a while. Reading the code at the pinned commit, only one of the four can actually be watched. The capacity gate has real data — about 1,200 completed items classified into buckets — and flipping it is a genuine decision. The judgment gates only write down *clearances*, never the times they fired, so you can count approvals but never work out how often the gate was wrong. The autonomy dial reads a log file that nothing in the codebase writes, so its numbers are permanently zero. The swarm-launch gate computes a setting and then throws it away on the next line; no gate clearance is ever checked there.

Two further problems make enforcement worse than the issue expects. A clearance is tied to a fingerprint of the exact file list it was granted for, so touching one more file invalidates it — on a repo whose main output is agent directives and skills, that means asking a human before nearly every push, including the push that documents the flip itself. And a clearance can be recorded by any agent typing a human's name into a free-text field; the one real record on disk is exactly that. So blocking mode would stop humans and CI while the agents it is aimed at can wave themselves through.
